issues.detail: The Greek 'αρον αρον' (aron aron) is an imperative meaning 'Lift him up!' or 'Take him up!', not 'Hãy cất đi!' (which means 'Remove it/them!' or 'Put it away!'). The Vietnamese translation loses the specific action of lifting Jesus up for inspection.

The Greek 'ουκ εχομεν βασιλεα ει μη καισαρα' means 'We have no king except Caesar.' The Vietnamese 'không có vua nào khác ngoài Sê-sa' (no other king besides Caesar) slightly shifts the logic, but more importantly, the Greek implies 'We have no king [other than] Caesar,' whereas the Vietnamese phrasing 'không có... nào khác ngoài' is a common construction, but the primary issue remains the 'aron aron' mistranslation.
